passages.text: In the thirty-sixth year of Asa’s reign, Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and fortified Ramah to prevent anyone from leaving or entering the territory of Asa king of Judah.
passages.sermon:
Asa was king of Judah.
Baasha was king of Israel.
In the thirty-sixth year of Asa’s reign, Baasha attacked Judah.
Baasha built up the city of Ramah.
Baasha wanted to control movement in and out of Judah.
Baasha tried to stop people from leaving or entering Asa’s territory.
passages.original: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וָשֵׁשׁ֙ לְמַלְכ֣וּת אָסָ֔א עָלָ֞ה בַּעְשָׁ֤א מֶֽלֶךְ־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עַל־ יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיִּ֖בֶן אֶת־ הָרָמָ֑ה לְבִלְתִּ֗י תֵּ֚ת יוֹצֵ֣א וָבָ֔א לְאָסָ֖א מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: So Asa withdrew the silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the LORD and the royal palace, and he sent it with this message to Ben-hadad king of Aram, who was ruling in Damascus: “Let there be a treaty between me and you, between my father and your father. See, I have sent you silver and gold. Now go and break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me.”
passages.sermon:
Asa was king of Judah.
He took silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
He also took silver and gold from the royal palace.
He sent this silver and gold to Ben-hadad.
Ben-hadad was king of Aram.
Ben-hadad lived in Damascus.
Asa sent a message to Ben-hadad.
He said, “Let there be a treaty between me and you.
There was a treaty between my father and your father.
I have sent you silver and gold.
Go and break your treaty with Baasha, king of Israel.
Then Baasha will leave me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּצֵ֨א אָסָ֜א כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֗ב מֵאֹֽצְר֛וֹת בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה וּבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח אֶל־ בֶּן־ הֲדַד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם הַיּוֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּדַרְמֶ֖שֶׂק לֵאמֹֽר׃ בְּרִית֙ בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֔ךָ וּבֵ֥ין אָבִ֖י וּבֵ֣ין אָבִ֑יךָ הִנֵּ֨ה שָׁלַ֤חְתִּֽי לְךָ֙ כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֔ב לֵ֞ךְ הָפֵ֣ר בְּרִֽיתְךָ֗ אֶת־ בַּעְשָׁא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְיַעֲלֶ֖ה מֵעָלָֽי׃

passages.text: And Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel, conquering Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and all the store cities of Naphtali.
passages.sermon:
Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
King Asa of Judah sent a message to Ben-hadad.
Ben-hadad listened to King Asa.
Ben-hadad sent the commanders of his armies.
He sent them to attack the cities of Israel.
The armies conquered Ijon.
They conquered Dan.
They conquered Abel-maim.
They conquered all the store cities of Naphtali.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֨ע בֶּן הֲדַ֜ד אֶל־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָסָ֗א וַ֠יִּשְׁלַח אֶת־ שָׂרֵ֨י הַחֲיָלִ֤ים אֲשֶׁר־ לוֹ֙ אֶל־ עָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּכּוּ֙ אֶת־ עִיּ֣וֹן וְאֶת־ דָּ֔ן וְאֵ֖ת אָבֵ֣ל מָ֑יִם וְאֵ֥ת כָּֽל־ מִסְכְּנ֖וֹת עָרֵ֥י נַפְתָּלִֽי׃

passages.text: When Baasha learned of this, he stopped fortifying Ramah and abandoned his work.
passages.sermon:
Baasha was the king of Israel.
Baasha heard what happened.
He learned that Ben-hadad attacked his cities.
He stopped building up the city of Ramah.
He left his work unfinished.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֙ כִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ בַּעְשָׁ֔א וַיֶּחְדַּ֕ל מִבְּנ֖וֹת אֶת־ הָרָמָ֑ה וַיַּשְׁבֵּ֖ת אֶת־ מְלַאכְתּֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: Then King Asa brought all the men of Judah, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and the timbers Baasha had used for building. And with these materials he built up Geba and Mizpah.
passages.sermon:
King Asa ruled over Judah.
King Asa gathered all the men of Judah.
The men of Judah carried away the stones from Ramah.
They also took the timbers from Ramah.
Baasha had used these stones and timbers to build.
King Asa used these materials.
He built up the city of Geba.
He also built up the city of Mizpah.
passages.original: וְאָסָ֣א הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ לָקַח֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיִּשְׂא֞וּ אֶת־ אַבְנֵ֤י הָֽרָמָה֙ וְאֶת־ עֵצֶ֔יהָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָ֖ה בַּעְשָׁ֑א וַיִּ֣בֶן בָּהֶ֔ם אֶת־ גֶּ֖בַע וְאֶת־ הַמִּצְפָּֽה׃ס

passages.text: At that time Hanani the seer came to King Asa of Judah and told him, “Because you have relied on the king of Aram and not on the LORD your God, the army of the king of Aram has escaped from your hand.
passages.sermon:
Hanani was a seer.
Hanani came to Asa.
Asa was the king of Judah.
Hanani spoke to Asa.
Hanani said, “You relied on the king of Aram.
You did not rely on the LORD your God.
Because of this, the army of the king of Aram escaped from your hand.”
passages.original: וּבָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא בָּ֚א חֲנָ֣נִי הָרֹאֶ֔ה אֶל־ אָסָ֖א מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו בְּהִשָּׁ֨עֶנְךָ֜ עַל־ מֶ֤לֶךְ אֲרָם֙ וְלֹ֤א נִשְׁעַ֙נְתָּ֙ עַל־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ עַל־ כֵּ֗ן נִמְלַ֛ט חֵ֥יל מֶֽלֶךְ־ אֲרָ֖ם מִיָּדֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Were not the Cushites and Libyans a vast army with many chariots and horsemen? Yet because you relied on the LORD, He delivered them into your hand.
passages.sermon:
The Cushites and the Libyans were a great army.
They had many chariots.
They had many horsemen.
They were very strong.
You relied on the LORD.
The LORD gave them into your hand.
passages.original: הֲלֹ֧א הַכּוּשִׁ֣ים וְהַלּוּבִ֗ים הָי֨וּ לְחַ֧יִל׀ לָרֹ֛ב לְרֶ֥כֶב וּלְפָרָשִׁ֖ים לְהַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וּבְהִשָּֽׁעֶנְךָ֥ עַל־ יְהוָ֖ה נְתָנָ֥ם בְּיָדֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: For the eyes of the LORD roam to and fro over all the earth, to show Himself strong on behalf of those whose hearts are fully devoted to Him. You have acted foolishly in this matter. From now on, therefore, you will be at war.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD sees everything.
His eyes roam throughout the whole earth.
He looks for people who are fully devoted to Him.
He shows His strength to those people.
You did not act wisely in this matter.
Because of this, you will have wars from now on.
passages.original: כִּ֣י יְהוָ֗ה עֵינָ֞יו מְשֹׁטְט֤וֹת בְּכָל־ הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ לְ֠הִתְחַזֵּק עִם־ לְבָבָ֥ם שָׁלֵ֛ם אֵלָ֖יו נִסְכַּ֣לְתָּ עַל־ זֹ֑את כִּ֣י מֵעַ֔תָּה יֵ֥שׁ עִמְּךָ֖ מִלְחָמֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Asa was angry with the seer and became so enraged over this matter that he put the man in prison. And at the same time Asa oppressed some of the people.
passages.sermon:
Asa was king of Judah.
Asa became angry with the seer.
The seer had spoken to Asa about his actions.
Asa was very enraged because of this matter.
Asa put the seer in prison.
At the same time, Asa oppressed some of the people.
passages.original: וַיִּכְעַ֨ס אָסָ֜א אֶל־ הָרֹאֶ֗ה וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֙הוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית הַמַּהְפֶּ֔כֶת כִּֽי־ בְזַ֥עַף עִמּ֖וֹ עַל־ זֹ֑את וַיְרַצֵּ֥ץ אָסָ֛א מִן־ הָעָ֖ם בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִֽיא׃

passages.text: Now the rest of the acts of Asa, from beginning to end, are indeed written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
passages.sermon:
Asa was a king of Judah.
Writers recorded Asa’s deeds.
They wrote about Asa’s early acts.
They wrote about Asa’s later acts.
They wrote these things in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
passages.original: וְהִנֵּה֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י אָסָ֔א הָרִאשׁוֹנִ֖ים וְהָאַחֲרוֹנִ֑ים הִנָּ֤ם כְּתוּבִים֙ עַל־ סֵ֣פֶר הַמְּלָכִ֔ים לִיהוּדָ֖ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: In the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa became diseased in his feet, and his malady became increasingly severe. Yet even in his illness he did not seek the LORD, but only the physicians.
passages.sermon:
Asa was king of Judah.
In the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa became sick in his feet.
His sickness grew worse and worse.
Even when Asa was very ill, he did not seek help from the LORD.
Asa only looked for help from the physicians.
passages.original: וַיֶּחֱלֶ֣א אָסָ֡א בִּשְׁנַת֩ שְׁלוֹשִׁ֨ים וָתֵ֤שַׁע לְמַלְכוּתוֹ֙ בְּרַגְלָ֔יו עַד־ לְמַ֖עְלָה חָלְי֑וֹ וְגַם־ בְּחָלְיוֹ֙ לֹא־ דָרַ֣שׁ אֶת־ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֖י בָּרֹפְאִֽים׃

passages.text: So in the forty-first year of his reign, Asa died and rested with his fathers.
passages.sermon: Asa was king of Judah.\r\nHe died in the forty-first year of his reign.\r\nHe rested with his fathers.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב אָסָ֖א עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֑יו וַיָּ֕מָת בִּשְׁנַ֛ת אַרְבָּעִ֥ים וְאַחַ֖ת לְמָלְכֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And he was buried in the tomb that he had cut out for himself in the City of David. They laid him on a bier that was full of spices and various blended perfumes; then they made a great fire in his honor.
passages.sermon:
Asa was king of Judah.
He died.
People buried Asa in the tomb he had prepared for himself.
This tomb was in the City of David.
They placed Asa on a bier.
The bier was filled with spices and mixed perfumes.
People made a very large fire to honor Asa.
passages.original: וַיִּקְבְּרֻ֣הוּ בְקִבְרֹתָ֗יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּֽרָה־ לוֹ֮ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִיד֒ וַיַּשְׁכִּיבֻ֗הוּ בַּמִּשְׁכָּב֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר מִלֵּא֙ בְּשָׂמִ֣ים וּזְנִ֔ים מְרֻקָּחִ֖ים בְּמִרְקַ֣חַת מַעֲשֶׂ֑ה וַיִּשְׂרְפוּ־ ל֥וֹ שְׂרֵפָ֖ה גְּדוֹלָ֥ה עַד־ לִמְאֹֽד׃פ
